nodes.name: Create Batch Context

parameters.query:
-- Open the run ledger entry BEFORE any data moves.
-- A crash after this point leaves a visible 'running' row rather than silence.
--
-- Window strategy: re-request the last successful window's final day (orders
-- arrive during the day, so yesterday's window was incomplete when it ran),
-- or backfill 180 days on a cold start. Overlap is safe because fact_orders
-- is keyed on order_id.
WITH last_success AS (
    SELECT max(window_to) AS last_to
    FROM salesops.ingestion_runs
    -- Scoped to this pipeline's own source. ingestion_runs is shared with the
    -- FX sync and the KPI refresh (Stage 4); without this filter their windows
    -- would be mistaken for ours and the next window would be computed wrong.
    WHERE source = 'mock-sales-api'
      AND status IN ('success', 'partial')
)
INSERT INTO salesops.ingestion_runs
    (batch_id, source, window_from, window_to, status, n8n_execution_id)
SELECT
    gen_random_uuid(),
    'mock-sales-api',
    COALESCE(
        (SELECT last_to FROM last_success) - INTERVAL '1 day',
        CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '180 days'
    )::date,
    CURRENT_DATE,
    'running',
    $1
RETURNING
    batch_id::text    AS batch_id,
    window_from::text AS window_from,
    window_to::text   AS window_to,
    run_id;

nodes.notes: Opens the ingestion_runs row as 'running' and computes this run's date window.

nodes.name: Stage Raw Orders

parameters.query:
-- Land every payload exactly as received, in one set-based statement.
-- The whole orders array arrives as a single JSONB parameter, so 4,000 orders
-- cost one round trip instead of 4,000.
--
-- No validation here by design: staging must be unable to reject anything,
-- or a malformed row has nowhere to land and the dead-letter trail is lost.
WITH landed AS (
    INSERT INTO salesops.raw_orders_staging (batch_id, order_id, source_payload)
    SELECT
        $1::uuid,
        o ->> 'order_id',
        o
    FROM jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) AS o
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT count(*)::int AS records_staged FROM landed;

nodes.notes: One set-based INSERT. Payloads land untouched - this is the traceability boundary.

nodes.name: Validate Orders

parameters.query:
-- Validate against the Stage 2 business rules and dead-letter the failures.
--
-- Every rule is evaluated for every row, so the error_message lists ALL the
-- reasons a record was rejected rather than only the first. Fixing one problem
-- and rediscovering the next on the next run wastes a cycle each time.
--
-- Casts go through salesops.try_to_* so that garbage input returns NULL rather
-- than raising and aborting the batch this statement exists to isolate.
WITH candidate AS (
    SELECT s.ingestion_id, s.source_payload AS p
    FROM salesops.raw_orders_staging s
    WHERE s.batch_id = $1::uuid
      AND s.processing_status = 'pending'
),
typed AS (
    SELECT
        c.ingestion_id,
        btrim(COALESCE(c.p ->> 'order_id', ''))    AS order_id,
        salesops.try_to_date(c.p ->> 'order_date') AS order_date,
        c.p ->> 'region'                           AS region_code,
        c.p ->> 'product'                          AS product_sku,
        c.p ->> 'channel'                          AS channel_code,
        btrim(COALESCE(c.p ->> 'customer_id', '')) AS customer_id,
        salesops.try_to_numeric(c.p ->> 'quantity')      AS quantity,
        salesops.try_to_numeric(c.p ->> 'unit_price')    AS unit_price,
        salesops.try_to_numeric(c.p ->> 'refund_amount') AS refund_amount,
        upper(btrim(COALESCE(c.p ->> 'currency', '')))   AS currency
    FROM candidate c
),
checked AS (
    SELECT
        t.ingestion_id,
        array_remove(ARRAY[
            CASE WHEN t.order_id = ''
                 THEN 'order_id is missing or empty' END,
            CASE WHEN t.order_date IS NULL
                 THEN 'order_date is missing or not a valid date' END,
            CASE WHEN t.order_date IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (
                     SELECT 1 FROM salesops.dim_date d WHERE d.calendar_date = t.order_date)
                 THEN 'order_date ' || t.order_date::text || ' is outside dim_date' END,
            CASE WHEN t.customer_id = ''
                 THEN 'customer_id is missing or empty' END,
            -- Unknown reference values are rejected, never auto-created. This is
            -- what makes reference-data drift visible instead of silently
            -- growing a dimension nobody agreed to.
            CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (
                     SELECT 1 FROM salesops.dim_region r WHERE r.region_code = t.region_code)
                 THEN 'unknown region: ' || COALESCE(t.region_code, '<null>') END,
            CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (
                     SELECT 1 FROM salesops.dim_product p2 WHERE p2.product_sku = t.product_sku)
                 THEN 'unknown product: ' || COALESCE(t.product_sku, '<null>') END,
            CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (
                     SELECT 1 FROM salesops.dim_channel ch WHERE ch.channel_code = t.channel_code)
                 THEN 'unknown channel: ' || COALESCE(t.channel_code, '<null>') END,
            CASE WHEN t.quantity IS NULL THEN 'quantity is missing or not numeric'
                 WHEN t.quantity <= 0   THEN 'quantity must be greater than zero' END,
            CASE WHEN t.unit_price IS NULL THEN 'unit_price is missing or not numeric'
                 WHEN t.unit_price < 0    THEN 'unit_price must not be negative' END,
            CASE WHEN t.refund_amount IS NULL THEN 'refund_amount is missing or not numeric'
                 WHEN t.refund_amount < 0    THEN 'refund_amount must not be negative' END,
            CASE WHEN t.refund_amount IS NOT NULL
                  AND t.quantity IS NOT NULL
                  AND t.unit_price IS NOT NULL
                  AND t.refund_amount > t.quantity * t.unit_price
                 THEN 'refund_amount exceeds gross amount' END,
            CASE WHEN t.currency !~ '^[A-Z]{3}$'
                 THEN 'currency is not a 3-letter ISO code: ' || COALESCE(NULLIF(t.currency, ''), '<null>')
                 WHEN t.currency NOT IN ('USD', 'EUR', 'GBP', 'JPY', 'BRL')
                 THEN 'unsupported currency: ' || t.currency END
        ]::text[], NULL) AS reasons
    FROM typed t
),
rejected AS (
    UPDATE salesops.raw_orders_staging s
    SET processing_status = 'failed',
        error_message     = array_to_string(c.reasons, '; '),
        processed_at      = now()
    FROM checked c
    WHERE s.ingestion_id = c.ingestion_id
      AND cardinality(c.reasons) > 0
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM rejected)::int                              AS records_rejected,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM checked WHERE cardinality(reasons) = 0)::int AS records_valid;

nodes.notes: Dead-letters invalid rows with every failing reason. Payload is left intact.

nodes.name: Resolve Customers

parameters.query:
-- dim_customer is a late-arriving dimension: customers exist because an order
-- referenced them, not because a customer feed was loaded first.
--
-- LEAST() on conflict means first_seen_date only ever moves earlier, so a
-- backfill of older orders corrects the value instead of corrupting it.
--
-- customer_name is deliberately not set. The orders API carries no name, and
-- fabricating one would put invented data in the warehouse.
WITH incoming AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.source_payload ->> 'customer_id')
        s.source_payload ->> 'customer_id'                    AS customer_id,
        r.region_id,
        salesops.try_to_date(s.source_payload ->> 'order_date') AS first_seen_date
    FROM salesops.raw_orders_staging s
    JOIN salesops.dim_region r
      ON r.region_code = s.source_payload ->> 'region'
    WHERE s.batch_id = $1::uuid
      AND s.processing_status = 'pending'
    ORDER BY
        s.source_payload ->> 'customer_id',
        salesops.try_to_date(s.source_payload ->> 'order_date')
),
upserted AS (
    INSERT INTO salesops.dim_customer (customer_id, region_id, first_seen_date)
    SELECT customer_id, region_id, first_seen_date FROM incoming
    ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE
        SET first_seen_date = LEAST(
                salesops.dim_customer.first_seen_date,
                EXCLUDED.first_seen_date)
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT count(*)::int AS customers_upserted FROM upserted;

nodes.notes: Late-arriving dimension upsert. first_seen_date only ever moves earlier.

nodes.name: Insert Facts

parameters.query:
-- Resolve source labels to surrogate keys by JOIN, then insert idempotently.
--
-- ON CONFLICT (order_id) DO NOTHING, not DO UPDATE: a placed order is an
-- immutable historical event. Re-reading the same window must never rewrite
-- what was already recorded, because a silent overwrite would destroy the
-- audit trail the staging layer exists to provide. Corrections belong in a
-- deliberate amendment process, not in a routine re-run.
--
-- Generated columns (gross_amount_local and the three USD amounts) are absent
-- from the column list - PostgreSQL rejects any attempt to write them.
WITH ready AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.source_payload ->> 'order_id')
        s.ingestion_id,
        s.source_payload ->> 'order_id'                          AS order_id,
        salesops.try_to_date(s.source_payload ->> 'order_date')  AS order_date,
        s.source_payload ->> 'customer_id'                       AS customer_id,
        r.region_id,
        p.product_id,
        c.channel_id,
        salesops.try_to_numeric(s.source_payload ->> 'quantity')::integer         AS quantity,
        salesops.try_to_numeric(s.source_payload ->> 'unit_price')::numeric(14,4) AS unit_price,
        upper(s.source_payload ->> 'currency')                                    AS currency,
        salesops.try_to_numeric(s.source_payload ->> 'refund_amount')::numeric(18,4) AS refund_amount_local
    FROM salesops.raw_orders_staging s
    JOIN salesops.dim_region  r ON r.region_code  = s.source_payload ->> 'region'
    JOIN salesops.dim_product p ON p.product_sku  = s.source_payload ->> 'product'
    JOIN salesops.dim_channel c ON c.channel_code = s.source_payload ->> 'channel'
    WHERE s.batch_id = $1::uuid
      AND s.processing_status = 'pending'
    ORDER BY s.source_payload ->> 'order_id', s.ingestion_id
),
inserted AS (
    INSERT INTO salesops.fact_orders (
        order_id, order_date, customer_id, region_id, product_id, channel_id,
        quantity, unit_price, currency, refund_amount_local)
    SELECT
        order_id, order_date, customer_id, region_id, product_id, channel_id,
        quantity, unit_price, currency, refund_amount_local
    FROM ready
    ON CONFLICT (order_id) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING order_id
),
-- Close out every pending row of the batch, including any duplicate order_ids
-- collapsed by DISTINCT ON above, so nothing is left stuck at 'pending'.
marked AS (
    UPDATE salesops.raw_orders_staging tgt
    SET processing_status = CASE WHEN i.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'processed' ELSE 'skipped' END,
        processed_at      = now()
    FROM salesops.raw_orders_staging src
    LEFT JOIN inserted i ON i.order_id = src.source_payload ->> 'order_id'
    WHERE tgt.ingestion_id = src.ingestion_id
      AND src.batch_id = $1::uuid
      AND src.processing_status = 'pending'
    RETURNING tgt.processing_status AS final_status
)
SELECT
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE final_status = 'processed')::int AS records_accepted,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE final_status = 'skipped')::int   AS records_duplicate
FROM marked;

nodes.notes: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Orders are immutable events; a re-run must not rewrite history.

nodes.name: Ensure USD Identity Rate

parameters.query:
-- USD -> USD is an identity, not a market rate, so recording it here is not
-- inventing FX. Without it every USD order would sit unconverted forever,
-- because Frankfurter never returns a USD/USD pair.
--
-- source = 'identity' keeps it distinguishable from anything fetched.
WITH added AS (
    INSERT INTO salesops.exchange_rates (rate_date, currency, rate_to_usd, source)
    SELECT d::date, 'USD', 1.0, 'identity'
    FROM generate_series($1::date, $2::date, INTERVAL '1 day') AS d
    ON CONFLICT (rate_date, currency) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT count(*)::int AS usd_rates_added FROM added;

nodes.notes: USD->USD = 1.0 is an identity, not invented FX. Frankfurter never returns this pair.

nodes.name: Attach Available FX

parameters.query:
-- Attach whatever rates already exist. Stage 3 does not fetch FX - the
-- Frankfurter sync is a separate workflow - so non-USD rows legitimately stay
-- NULL here and their USD amounts stay NULL with them.
--
-- Setting exchange_rate_to_usd is all that is needed: gross/refund/net USD are
-- generated columns and recompute themselves. Nothing writes a money value
-- twice, so nothing can drift out of step with its rate.
--
-- Only fills rows that have no rate yet, so a corrected rate is never
-- overwritten by a routine re-run.
WITH applied AS (
    UPDATE salesops.fact_orders f
    SET exchange_rate_to_usd = x.rate_to_usd
    FROM salesops.exchange_rates x
    WHERE x.rate_date = f.order_date
      AND x.currency  = f.currency
      AND f.exchange_rate_to_usd IS NULL
      AND f.order_date BETWEEN $1::date AND $2::date
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT count(*)::int AS fx_applied FROM applied;

nodes.notes: Applies existing rates only. Non-USD rows stay NULL until the Frankfurter sync exists.

nodes.name: Finalize Ingestion Run

parameters.query:
-- Close the run. status is derived, never asserted: a run that rejected
-- anything is 'partial', so a green tick can never hide a dead-letter pile.
-- The counts-balance CHECK on ingestion_runs rejects arithmetic that does not
-- add up, which turns a silent pipeline bug into a loud constraint violation.
UPDATE salesops.ingestion_runs r
SET finished_at       = now(),
    records_received  = $2::int,
    records_accepted  = $3::int,
    records_rejected  = $4::int,
    records_duplicate = $5::int,
    status            = CASE WHEN $4::int > 0 THEN 'partial' ELSE 'success' END
WHERE r.batch_id = $1::uuid
RETURNING
    run_id,
    batch_id::text    AS batch_id,
    window_from::text AS window_from,
    window_to::text   AS window_to,
    status,
    records_received,
    records_accepted,
    records_rejected,
    records_duplicate,
    round(extract(epoch FROM (finished_at - started_at))::numeric, 2) AS duration_seconds,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM salesops.fact_orders f
      WHERE f.exchange_rate_to_usd IS NULL
        AND f.order_date BETWEEN r.window_from AND r.window_to)::int AS orders_awaiting_fx;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ $('Validate API Response').first().json.batch_id, $('Validate API Response').first().json.records_received || 0, $('Insert Facts').first().json.records_accepted || 0, $('Validate Orders').first().json.records_rejected || 0, $('Insert Facts').first().json.records_duplicate || 0 ] }}

nodes.notes: Derives success vs partial from the counts. Never asserts success.
